physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (tobe, boubou, riga), composed of 67 uniform strips of hand-spun cotton, made by the Yoruba using a mixture of sanyan silk and white cotton arranged in warp-faced stripes. These have been hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips on the body are aligned vertically, while the sleeves are arranged horizontally so as to flare out at the top. A large pocket has been sewn onto the breast, and this and the surrounding areas have been embroidered in the two knives (aska biyu) pattern in cream coloured cotton, with a large spiral on both the front and back of the tunic. The tunic is lined around the neck and the sleeves with indigo-dyed cotton and has been hemmed.
